classification.difficultyReason: Part c requires selecting overlapping triangles, finding the full isosceles vertex angle and a smaller triangle angle, then subtracting to isolate the requested angle.

content.prompt: Find the value of $\alpha$ in each of these diagrams.

spec.description: Triangle ABC between parallel lines EABF and GCH, with matching arrow marks.
spec.mathematics: Angle ACB is 44 degrees; angle BCH is 54 degrees; alpha is BAC.

answer.worked:
$\angle ABC=54^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CH$).

$\begin{align*}\alpha+54^\circ+44^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=82^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of $\triangle ABC$.

spec.description: Parallel horizontal lines BC and EF; BF and CE meet at A. Curved leader retains the association of 37 degrees with B.
spec.mathematics: CBA is 37 degrees, CAF is 110 degrees, alpha is AEF.

answer.worked:
$\angle EAF=70^\circ$ (adjacent angles on straight line $CAE$).

$\angle AFE=37^\circ$ (alternate angles, $BC\parallel EF$).

$\begin{align*}\alpha+70^\circ+37^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=73^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of $\triangle AEF$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral ABCD with intersecting diagonals, AB=BC ticks and curved angle leaders.
spec.mathematics: BAC=16 degrees, BXA=92 degrees, BDC=37 degrees; alpha is CBD.

answer.short:
$\alpha=76^\circ$.

Use the equal base angles of $\triangle ABC$, then subtract $\angle ABX$.
answer.worked:
$\angle ACB=16^\circ$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle ABC$, $AB=BC$).

$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=180^\circ-16^\circ-16^\circ\\\angle ABC&=148^\circ\\\angle ABX&=180^\circ-16^\circ-92^\circ\\\angle ABX&=72^\circ\\\alpha&=148^\circ-72^\circ\\\alpha&=76^\circ\end{align*}$

Use the angle sums of $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ABX$, then adjacent angles at $B$.
